name: South Africa
shortSummary: India and South Africa share a historic bond dating to Mahatma Gandhi's formative years in South Africa (1893-1914), and today cooperate closely through BRICS, IBSA, and shared Global South advocacy.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Shared anti-colonial and anti-apartheid legacy anchors deep political trust.
South Africa is a major supplier of gold, coal and manganese to India.

recentDevelopments.title: Continued BRICS and Global South coordination
recentDevelopments.description: India and South Africa continued close coordination within BRICS (including on its 2024 expansion) and other Global South forums.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Reinforces the historic political trust underpinning one of India's closest African partnerships.

historicalEvents.title: Gandhi's Arrival in South Africa
historicalEvents.description: Mohandas Gandhi arrives in South Africa, where over the next two decades he develops the philosophy and tactics of nonviolent resistance later central to India's independence movement.

historicalEvents.title: Restoration of Full Diplomatic Relations
historicalEvents.description: India and South Africa restore full diplomatic relations following the end of apartheid, having supported the anti-apartheid movement for decades.

historicalEvents.title: IBSA Dialogue Forum Founded
historicalEvents.description: India, Brazil and South Africa launch the IBSA grouping to coordinate Global South positions.

defenceCooperation.name: IBSAMAR
defenceCooperation.description: Trilateral naval exercise between India, Brazil and South Africa.
